mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. Prior path: 13.25% held at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug); 25bps cut from 13.50% at the May 2026 MPC; 75bps cut from 14.25% on 11 Feb 2026. The 30 Sep decision coincided with the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect and the start of IMF successor-programme talks.

trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha continued to drift weaker in early October, with the USD/ZMW market mid at ~K19.7465/USD (open.er-api.com, 5 Oct) versus ~K19.63 at the start of the month — a further ~0.6% softening that keeps the pair near the top of its recent range. The move was a broad, basket-wide grind rather than a one-pair spike: GBP (26.3013, +0.87%), EUR (22.5271, +0.99%), BWP (1.4061, +1.06%), ZAR (1.205, +0.41%) and USD (19.7465, +0.61%) all cost more ZMW, while CNY (2.9386) was flat. With the USD/ZMW mid now testing the upper edge of the broad 18.40–19.80 consolidation band, the recent direction has flipped from the sharp H1 appreciation to a mild seasonal softening. The policy backdrop remains the 30 September 250bps MPR cut to 10.75% — the lowest in several years — which trims the carry support that buoyed the kwacha earlier in 2026. Import demand, softer copper-price swings and the pace of further BoZ easing are the near-term risks; IMF successor-programme talks and the 2027 budget shape the medium-term path.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
